source.title: SageBwd: A Trainable Low-bit Attention
source.authors: Jintao Zhang; Marco Chen; Hao-Xu Wang; Kai Jiang; Ion Stoica; Joseph Gonzalez; Jian-Fei Chen; Jun Zhu

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch size/tokens per step and QK-norm affect pretraining performance of low-bit attention relative to full-precision attention, a new setting for the listed generalization-gap versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies quantization error and pretraining loss, not fitting arbitrary labels or test error on natural labels. Its training-loss comparisons and intermediate-tensor measurements do not measure the behavior named in V1–V8. Cited results about large-batch training are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study reports pretraining loss, training stability and quantization fidelity, without identifying any loss as held-out evaluation or measuring a training–test gap. Its batch-size experiments therefore do not test V5. Keskar et al. is cited as background on batch size and gradient noise; none of V1–V8 is tested or used as an evaluated tool.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that QK-norm stabilizes high-TPS SageBwd training, the low-magnitude dS path is the principal quantization bottleneck, and smaller TPS permits FPA-level pretraining loss. They also conclude that K-smoothing remains essential while Q-smoothing has limited benefit. The explanation involving gradient noise masking quantization error is a hypothesis, not an established causal result.
record.recipe_differences: Studies low-bit attention quantization and pretraining loss, rather than arbitrary-label memorization, natural-label held-out error, or the listed generalization measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Tokens per step (varied through global batch size with sequence length fixed), QK-norm, K-smoothing and Q-smoothing affect training stability, pretraining loss or quantization fidelity.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 78B-token budget, SageBwd versus FPA losses are 2.640 versus 2.586 at 2.1M tokens per step, and 2.561 versus 2.563 at 260K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing batch size closes SageBwd's pretraining-loss deficit relative to FPA in this 325M Llama setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing QK-norm causes divergence at high tokens per step but permits FPA-level pretraining performance at low tokens per step. K-smoothing remains necessary; Q-smoothing gives no consistent benefit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization and smoothing choices condition the stability and numerical fidelity of low-bit attention pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic Q/K scale increases degrade gradient fidelity, and checkpoint analysis identifies the low-magnitude dS path and downstream dQ/dK as numerical bottlenecks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-bit attention is particularly sensitive to quantization error along the softmax-gradient path.

record.problems: The TPS analysis varies global batch size only, holds sequence length fixed and leaves sequence-length interactions for future work. Some quantitative intermediate-error analysis uses a pseudo-quantized FPA baseline with dO treated as error-free. The supplied excerpt does not provide numerical uncertainty estimates for reported comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Appendix C figure-only layerwise comparisons were not separately extracted because the supplied text gives figure captions but no described numerical or textual outcomes for individual plotted conditions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural and random labels.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, and whether recipe changes remove a held-out penalty.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized versus random training examples and measuring test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification. A fixed token budget and a batch-size comparison alone do not establish V5: the reported outcome must measure held-out performance. Numerical gradient error also does not measure V7's weight-perturbation sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out generalization on natural and random labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and image test error.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and held-out performance.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training–test error gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
